acceptanceCriteria.text: The change extends `fetch-to-spec` on both SCM implementers in the same ship. No new intent id is added. The provider-specific allowlist stays empty.
GitHub `fetch-to-spec` extracts image and user-attachment URLs from the issue body and every comment (markdown images, HTML `img`, and `github.com/user-attachments/` file links).
Azure DevOps `fetch-to-spec` extracts image and attachment URLs from Description HTML, Acceptance Criteria HTML, `AttachedFile` relations, and WIT comments.
URL discovery may differ by host. Download, naming, manifest schema, Visual References shape, failure policy, and register copy are identical for GitHub and Azure DevOps.
Both converters call one shared ingest helper under `{sharedDir}/scripts/` that writes `{specsDir}/{specStem}.assets/` where `{specStem}` is the spec filename without `.spec.md`.
Each saved file is named `{NN}-{kind}-{sanitized-stem}{ext}` with `NN` starting at `01`. Kind is `screenshot`, `template`, `example`, `inline`, `comment`, or `attached`.

Kind prefers alt-text or original-filename keywords (`screenshot`/`print`, `template`/`mock`/`wireframe`, `example`/`sample`). Else origin maps body→`inline`, comment→`comment`, relation→`attached`. Unlabeled images default to `screenshot`.
Downloads reuse provider `validate-auth` credentials (GitHub token from `gh`/env, ADO PAT from the configured env var). Auth failure still STOPs the whole fetch with no silent GitHub↔Azure fallback.
URLs outside the GitHub user-attachment/user-image host allowlist or the ADO `{apiBase}` WIT attachments API are skipped as `disallowed-host`.
Per-file size above 10 MiB or run total above 50 MiB is skipped as `size-limit` without failing `fetch-to-spec`.
HTTP 404, 403, or timeout on one URL records `failed` in the manifest and leaves `fetch-to-spec` exit 0 when the spec file was written.
After at least one `ok` image, the spec of record contains `## Visual References` with repo-relative markdown images plus a table of path, kind, origin, and caption.
Zero `ok` assets means no assets directory, no Visual References heading, and `fetch-to-spec` still succeeds.
`register_local_spec.cjs` copies `{specsDir}/{specStem}.assets/` to `{us-dir}/attachments/` when the source assets directory exists.
`ws-spec-write` Reads each `ok` image during reformulation and writes observed UI, layout, or template constraints into Description, ACs, or Notes.
`ws-plan-write`, `ws-plan-interview`, and `ws-implement-tasks` SKILL.md require reading Visual References images before planning or editing product files when that heading exists.
`FORMAT.md` documents optional `## Visual References`. Specs without that heading still pass `--mode=compat`.
The `fetch-to-spec` row in `scm-provider-contract.md` states that inbound fetch downloads visual attachments when present and writes the shared assets sidecar plus Visual References.
Both provider `INTENTS.md` `## \`fetch-to-spec\`` procedures include the ingest step with the same output paths. `node test/test-provider-parity.js` exits 0.
The parity test asserts both INTENTS `fetch-to-spec` sections mention the assets sidecar (or `Visual References`) so a one-sided doc change fails CI.
Disallowed MIME (`image/svg+xml`, HTML, executables) is skipped as `disallowed-type`. Allowed types are `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, and `application/pdf`.
PDF files appear in Visual References as file links, not markdown images, and are not vision-analyzed.
ADO `clean_html` converts `` to markdown images before tag strip so Original Issue Context keeps local rewritten paths after ingest.
Offline `--input` still extracts URLs and attempts download when auth exists. Unreachable URLs are `skipped` or `failed` without aborting conversion.

Fixture tests with a mock HTTP layer cover **both** converters and assert renamed files, manifest fields (`sha256`, `kind`, `origin`, `status`), rewritten spec links, and fetch success when one URL 404s.
`ws-spec-from-provider` inherits ingest through `fetch-to-spec`. The bulk skill adds no second downloader.
`ws-cleanup` must not delete `{specsDir}/{specStem}.assets/`. `{us-dir}/attachments/` remains a plan artifact eligible for plan-dir cleanup.
`FEATURES.md` § SCM provider parity describes visual attachment ingest as part of `fetch-to-spec`, not as a separate intent.
